input.reasoning:
Estimate derived from story points using a velocity-based conversion (1 point ≈ 6-7 effort-hours, distributed across roles per task type), then costed against the given rate card. No historical actuals exist for this team, so point-to-hour ratios are assumption-based industry norms (bench-marked against similar Angular/API/Stripe/RBAC/data-migration work). Role hours were sized to respect FTE capacity over an assumed 3-month (~13-week) delivery window: Backend 1.5 FTE (~780h), Frontend 1.0 FTE (~520h), QA 0.6 FTE (~312h), DevOps 0.4 FTE (~208h). Total backlog points = 81, which is heavy relative to staffing (especially Backend and QA), so hours were allocated by task priority/complexity and capped near available capacity, with a note that the backlog exceeds comfortable capacity for the given team over one quarter — either timeline extends or scope must be trimmed.

Non-labour costs include Stripe integration sandbox/compliance overhead, a data-migration environment (Oracle read replica, migration tooling), and staging/CI infrastructure costs. A 12% contingency scenario and P50/P75/P90 scenarios are provided to reflect estimation uncertainty, especially around PW-8 (legacy migration) and PW-7 (payment integration/webhook reconciliation) which carry higher technical risk.

Reductions target the largest, most deferrable/negotiable cost drivers: descoping PW-2 (design system) to a minimal component set now, trimming QA regression hours by risk-based test selection, and phasing legacy migration (PW-8) to migrate only active-customer records first, deferring full historical invoice-line migration to a later phase.

scenarios.name: P50 - Base case (as scoped, full backlog)
P90 - Adverse case (migration/Stripe complexity, timeline slip)

nonLabourLines.description: Staging/CI cloud infrastructure (CI runners, staging environment hosting) for ~3 months
Stripe integration setup, sandbox/test transaction fees, and webhook monitoring tooling
Legacy Oracle read-replica / migration tooling licenses for data migration effort
PDF generation/storage service for invoice detail view
Contingency reserve (~12% of labour cost) for scope/estimation uncertainty

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; hour estimates are derived from story points using an assumed ~6-7 effort-hours-per-point conversion, not from past velocity.
Delivery window assumed at ~3 months (13 weeks), against which FTE capacity (Backend 1.5, Frontend 1.0, QA 0.6, DevOps 0.4) was used to cap realistic role hours.

Total backlog (81 points) is heavy relative to available capacity, particularly Backend Developer and QA Engineer; either the timeline extends beyond 3 months or scope (e.g. PW-8 migration) is phased.

PW-8 (legacy migration of 400k records/2M invoice lines) is assumed to require significant Backend + DevOps effort for ETL scripting, validation, and reconciliation, and carries the highest cost uncertainty.
PW-7 (Stripe integration) assumed to include webhook handling and reconciliation logic, tested by QA against sandbox transactions.
QA Engineer effort is assumed proportionate at ~0.6 FTE and focused on the Urgent/High priority items (PW-1, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5, PW-7, PW-8), with lighter coverage on Medium items (PW-2, PW-6).
DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) hours are concentrated on PW-1 (CI/staging setup) and support for PW-7/PW-8 environment needs.
Non-labour costs are rough order-of-magnitude estimates for typical cloud/tooling/service costs; actual vendor quotes were not provided.
Contingency of ~12% applied to labour cost to account for estimation uncertainty given lack of historical actuals.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal set of core components (buttons, forms, tables) now, deferring theming tokens and dialogs to a later phase
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~120h on PW-2

reductions.description: Phase PW-8 legacy migration: migrate active-customer records and recent invoice lines only in this phase, defer full historical 2M invoice-line migration to a follow-up project
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend Developer and DevOps Engineer hours allocated to PW-8 migration scripting/validation by roughly half

reductions.description: Apply risk-based (rather than full regression) QA testing strategy across Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6)
Defer non-essential non-labour spend (PDF service, part of migration tooling licenses) until later phase
reductions.effect: Removes/delays PDF generation service and reduces migration tooling license scope
